clue.text: One takes an interest in others' finances

definitions.text: One takes an interest in others' finances

parts.words: One takes an interest in others' finances
parts.note: taking an interest here means charging interest on a loan, not being curious about someone's money

explanation.surface: A nosy person who likes to know how other people are doing with their money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes an interest' reads as curiosity; the cryptic sense is collecting interest on money lent out.
explanation.definitionFit: A lender of money profits by charging interest on the sums borrowed by other people.

clue.text: One of the great composers — most are disturbed

indicators.note: letters disturbed are thrown out of place and rearranged

explanation.surface: A claim that most of the great composers are mentally troubled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges MOST and ARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestro is a title of respect for a distinguished conductor or composer.

clue.text: Upset, number one with bronze in race

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters read upwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
tan is a bronze, sun-darkened skin colour

explanation.surface: Disappointment for the winner who only took the bronze medal in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reads NOITAN upwards. 'race' means a people, not a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A race in the sense of a people of common descent is close to a nation.

clue.text: Definitely rare, yet damaged in the past

parts.note: yes is an emphatic affirmation, definitely

indicators.note: letters damaged are knocked out of shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: Something certainly rare, yet harmed long ago, like an antique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges RARE and YET into TERYEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Yesteryear is a literary word for times gone by, years ago.

clue.text: Burning energy to knock out one's groove

indicators.note: to knock something out is to displace it, so one letter replaces another

parts.note: a burning desire is an itch
I is the Roman numeral for one
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Fiery energy used to break someone out of their rut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to knock out' has E replace the I of ITCH. 'groove' means a cut line, not a rhythm.
explanation.definitionFit: An etch is a line incised by acid into a surface, a kind of groove.

clue.text: Many do watercolours of Belgium with black alders spreading around

indicators.note: letters spreading around scatter into a new arrangement

parts.note: B is the international vehicle code for Belgium
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Amateur painters depicting Belgian scenery with dark alder trees sprawling about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spreading around' rearranges B, B and ALDERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Dabblers are amateurs who try something casually, as many hobbyists do with watercolour painting.

clue.text: Roll 'To Sir, With Love' — interrupted by time for dinner?

indicators.note: to be interrupted by something is to have it break in, so one piece goes inside the other
to roll something is to turn it over, so these words are read backwards

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Someone playing the film 'To Sir, With Love' while being called away for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roll' turns TO SIR into RISOT; with O added, 'interrupted by' puts T inside to give RISOTTO. 'Roll' looks like a bread roll for dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian rice dish, an example of a dinner, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Coins from Spain found in packing-cases

indicators.note: a thing found in something else sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: crates are wooden packing-cases
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: Spanish money discovered stashed in shipping crates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coins' looks like a noun for money, but it is the verb meaning invents.
explanation.definitionFit: To coin a word or phrase is to invent it, so coins is a synonym of makes up or originates.

clue.text: People undertaking work — do they make reductions?

definitions.meaning: firms or individuals hired to carry out a job
things that contract shrink, so ... would be makers of reductions

explanation.surface: A question about whether builders lower their prices.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is whimsical: a contractor as one who contracts, making things smaller.
explanation.definitionFit: Builders and other hired tradespeople take on work under contract; to contract also means to reduce.

clue.text: They made art beginners should collect first

indicators.note: to collect something is to gather it in, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: cubs are novices, as in a cub reporter
1st, written IST, is the abbreviation of first

explanation.surface: Advice to novices that they should pick up some knowledge before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: First is written as the abbreviation 1st, with the numeral 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Cubists such as Picasso and Braque were painters of an early twentieth-century movement in art.

clue.text: One encourages colleagues to go all out?

definitions.text: One encourages colleagues to go all out?

parts.words: One encourages colleagues to go all out?
parts.note: to go all out sounds like giving maximum effort, but here it means everyone walking out on strike

explanation.surface: A motivating figure urging workmates to give their very best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go all out' reads as trying hard, but the cryptic sense is the whole workforce going out on strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop steward is a union representative elected by fellow workers, who might call them out on strike.

clue.text: Sting's fourth element in 'Every Breath You Take'

definitions.text: Sting's fourth element in 'Every Breath You Take'

parts.words: Sting's fourth element in 'Every Breath You Take'
parts.note: the fourth letter of the word Sting is N, the chemical symbol of a gas making up most of the air we breathe

explanation.surface: Pop trivia: what is the fourth ingredient in Sting's hit song 'Every Breath You Take'?
explanation.walkthrough: The song title belongs to Sting's band The Police, but here it is literal: the gas present in every breath. Sting's fourth letter, N, is that gas's chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrogen is the chemical element that forms about four fifths of air, so it is in each breath inhaled.

clue.text: Fortune's presented by bishop to drunk

indicators.note: a piece presented by another comes after it, so the bishop goes first

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
Fortune's reads as fortune is; lot means one's fortune or destiny

explanation.surface: A bishop hands a fortune to a drunkard.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s on Fortune stands for is, a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Blotto is British slang for extremely intoxicated, completely sozzled.

clue.text: Daughter comes in plastered — resolving this could get her higher!

indicators.note: resolving means breaking down and reforming, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A daughter arrives home drunk; sorting that out might cheer her up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes in' adds D to PLASTERED; 'resolving' rearranges them. 'plastered' looks like drunk, and 'higher' like being high.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepladder is a folding ladder that lets a person reach a higher shelf or ceiling.

clue.text: Source of river also flowing over

indicators.note: flowing back over itself suggests the word runs from right to left

parts.note: too means also

explanation.surface: The head of a river, which also overflows its banks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Source' looks like part of the river picture but is the definition; 'flowing over' signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: The root of something is its origin or cause, the place from which it springs.

clue.text: Cryptic variable in Times — ours better organised!

indicators.note: letters better organised have been rearranged into a new order

parts.note: Y is a conventional algebraic variable

explanation.surface: A boast that our crossword is better arranged than the one in The Times newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better organised' rearranges Y, TIMES and OURS together.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic describes something with a hidden or puzzling meaning, much like something enigmatic.

clue.text: Strong drink and ecstasy really tucked into by journalists

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: a thing tucked into by another has that piece put inside it

parts.note: so means really, as in so good
the press is the body of journalists

explanation.surface: Reporters eagerly downing alcohol and drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strong drink' suggests alcohol, but it is concentrated coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: Espresso is a concentrated coffee, a strong drink made by forcing steam through ground beans.

clue.text: Cheats using wits to secrete note

indicators.note: to secrete is to hide away, so one piece is concealed within the other

parts.note: a card is old slang for a witty, amusing person
a sharp is a note raised by a semitone

explanation.surface: Cheats use their cleverness to hide a slip of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' looks like a written message; it is the musical sharp.
explanation.definitionFit: Card-sharps are swindlers who win at card games by sleight of hand.

clue.text: Regret outspoken insult, being a bit of a fool?

indicators.note: outspoken means spoken out, so the word is given by how it sounds

parts.note: to rue is to regret
a barb is a cutting remark or insult

explanation.surface: Someone sorry for blurting out an insult and looking silly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit of a fool' is the fruit used in a fool, a British pudding of stewed fruit folded into cream.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhubarb fool is a classic version of the creamy dessert, so the stalk is one ingredient of it.

clue.text: Be at home on stage, with a different sound

definitions.meaning: to ... somewhere is to reside there, the verb rhyming with give

definitions.text: on stage, with a different sound
definitions.meaning: this adjective rhymes with hive, so it sounds different

explanation.surface: An actor who feels at ease performing in front of an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses share the spelling but not the vowel sound, which the clue flags.
explanation.definitionFit: Residing somewhere is the verb sense; a performance in front of an audience is the adjective sense.

clue.text: Wedding vow lies in ruins — is this love?

parts.note: I do is the vow said at a wedding

indicators.note: something in ruins is wrecked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A marriage promise broken by deceit raises the question of whether it was love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in ruins' rearranges LIES into LISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To idolise someone is to adore or worship them, an extreme form of love.

clue.text: Hostile Mexican gila monster eats while climbing

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means reading upwards, so the letters are reversed
the phrase eats the answer, holding it inside its letters

explanation.surface: An aggressive Mexican lizard feeding while scaling a rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eats' gives NGILAM within the phrase and 'while climbing' turns it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Malign means harmful or ill-disposed, as in malign intent, close to hostile.

clue.text: Work with plan to axe man

indicators.note: to axe something is to cut it out, so these letters are removed

parts.note: a manoeuvre is a scheme or plan
taken as written

explanation.surface: A workplace plan to sack an employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to axe' removes MAN from MANOEUVRE.
explanation.definitionFit: An oeuvre is the body of work produced by an artist or writer, borrowed from French.

clue.text: Dramatic, as an ovation engulfs Romeo

indicators.note: the phrase engulfs the answer, which lies within its run of letters

explanation.surface: A theatrical moment as the cheering of the audience swamps the actor playing Romeo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romeo' sounds like Shakespeare's hero in the theatre scene, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Romeo and Casanova are both bywords for a lover or womaniser.

clue.text: Motivate staff under pressure

indicators.note: in a down answer a piece under another comes after it

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: A boss spurring on employees who are under stress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like employees but is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: To prod is to poke or urge someone into action, to spur them on.

clue.text: Not so dense, small son embracing Eminem's music over Queen

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in the arms, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothes labels
S is the abbreviation for son in genealogies

indicators.note: turned over means the word is read backwards

parts.note: Eminem is a rapper, so his music is rap
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the late Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A young child holding a hip-hop record rather than Queen's rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' looks like the rock band set against Eminem, but gives ER; 'over' signals the reversal and 'embracing' the containment by the two S's.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparser is the comparative of sparse, meaning more thinly scattered, the opposite of denser.

clue.text: Made an icon facing two ways

definitions.meaning: to make someone an icon is to treat them as a god
the word is a palindrome, reading the same in both directions like a two-faced Janus

explanation.surface: An object made into an image of worship that looks both forwards and backwards, like Janus.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense describes the word's own spelling: it reads identically from either end.
explanation.definitionFit: To deify someone is to treat them as a god, an idol worshipped like an icon; the letters are palindromic.

clue.text: British ladies maybe with party spread food

parts.note: the ladies is a public toilet, an example of a loo
a do is a party or social event
a range is a spread or variety of things

explanation.surface: British women bringing dishes for a buffet at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' looks like the food at the party but gives RANGE; 'food' alone is the definition. LOO is British slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A blood orange is a citrus fruit with red flesh, an example of food.
